# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I hold the manual. The rule is clear: printed markings are bait — the only safe cut depends on the *light* color, not whatever the bomb prints. My table:

- blue light → cut yellow
- green light → cut green
- red light → cut red

I can't see the bomb and can't touch it. Deaf can see the bomb (light color) but can't touch. Blind can touch/work the parts but can't see colors. So the chain must be: Deaf sees the light color, tells me (but I can't hear and Deaf can't speak... wait — Deaf can't hear or speak? Deaf can see and presumably can gesture). Let me re-check the table.

- Deaf: can see the bomb, cannot hear or touch. So Deaf can gesture.
- Mute (me): can read manual, cannot speak or touch. I can gesture.
- Blind: can touch, cannot see.

So communication: Deaf can gesture → who sees gestures? "Whoever can see receives it." Blind cannot see. I (Mute) can see gestures. So Deaf gestures the light color to me. I read the manual, determine the cut wire color, and gesture it to... Blind can't see gestures. Hmm.

Wait — Blind can hear. I can't speak. Deaf can't speak either. So how does the cut color reach Blind?

Let me reconsider. Speech: "Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures." Deaf cannot hear. Blind can hear. Mute (me) cannot speak. So I cannot send words to Blind.

But Deaf can speak? No — Deaf "cannot hear anything." The table says Deaf cannot hear, but can Deaf speak? The monkey names: Deaf, Mute, Blind. Deaf = can't hear. Mute = can't speak. So Deaf CAN speak! Deaf can see the bomb and can speak.

So: Deaf sees light color, speaks it. Who hears? Blind can hear, and I (Mute) can hear? Wait, can Mute hear? Mute can't speak but presumably can hear. Yes — Mute reads manual, can hear.

So Deaf speaks the light color → I hear it, Blind hears it too. I read manual → I need to tell Blind the cut color. I can't speak, but I can gesture. Blind can't see gestures. Problem.

Hmm, but Blind can hear. So I need someone who can speak to relay to Blind. Deaf can speak. So I gesture the cut color to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to Blind. 

Actually simpler: Deaf sees light, speaks light color aloud (both Blind and I hear). I consult manual, gesture cut color to Deaf, Deaf speaks cut color to Blind, Blind cuts.

But wait — do I even need to be in the loop via gesture? I could gesture to Deaf. Deaf receives gestures (Deaf can see). Yes.

Let me just start the chain. Turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. I'm Mute, I go first. I haven't heard anything yet. I should tell them the rule so they know what to send me.

I can gesture to Deaf. Blind can't see gestures, but Blind can hear speech — I can't speak. So my only output is gesture to Deaf.

So I'll gesture to Deaf: explain the rule and ask for the light color. But gestures are symbols from the alphabet only — I can't encode arbitrary text easily. Hmm. The gesture alphabet is emoji. I need to convey meaning. "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something."

I need to establish a code. Let me think about what's minimal. I need Deaf to tell me the light color. Three options: blue, green, red. I could pre-agree: 👍 = blue, 👎 = green, 👌 = red? But Deaf doesn't know my code yet.

Actually, maybe I should just wait and let Deaf speak first? Deaf goes last in the round. Deaf can speak — Deaf could speak the light color aloud, and I'd hear it next round. Then I gesture the answer to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to Blind.

But Deaf doesn't know the rule yet. Deaf might just speak the printed color (the bait). That would be bad — but speaking isn't cutting, so no detonation. Only the cut matters. So Deaf speaking the printed color is harmless as long as Blind doesn't cut on it.

Hmm, but Blind might cut based on what Blind hears. Blind hears Deaf's speech. If Deaf says "the bomb shows red" (printed), Blind might cut red. That's the bait → detonation.

I must warn them. I can only gesture to Deaf. Let me gesture a warning and a code.

Let me design: I'll gesture to Deaf a sequence meaning "do not cut on printed color; tell me the LIGHT color." But encoding that in emoji is hard. 

Alternative: Since Deaf can see the bomb, Deaf sees both the light and the printed markings. The manual says printed = bait. So the light is the real signal. I need Deaf to report the light color.

Let me just establish a simple code and hope Deaf interprets. Actually, the cleanest: gesture the three color-codes and let Deaf map. But Deaf needs to know which is which.

Maybe I'm overcomplicating. Let me use gestures as a count/pointer. Actually, let me think about what Deaf already knows: Deaf sees the bomb. Deaf sees a light color and printed markings. Deaf might not know the rule.

I think the best first move: gesture to Deaf a clear "stop/attention" then a code. Let me pick a natural mapping and state it. Since gestures can't carry words, but the puzzle expects us to build meaning.

Let me try: I'll gesture to Deaf: ✋ (stop) then three gestures representing blue/green/red in a fixed order, then ☝ (point/one). Hmm, ambiguous.

Actually — reconsider. Maybe I should speak? No, I'm Mute, I cannot speak. Only gesture.

Let me reconsider the whole channel. Actually maybe the intended flow: Deaf sees light, gestures it to me (Mute). I read manual, gesture cut color to Deaf. Deaf speaks cut color to Blind. Blind cuts. And I also need to make sure Blind doesn't act on printed info.

For turn 1, I should send Deaf a message establishing the protocol. Let me gesture a warning and ask for light color.

I'll gesture: ✋ (stop — don't act on print), then 👁? no eye in alphabet. Hmm.

Let me just do something reasonable and iterate. I'll gesture to Deaf: ✋ ☝ and then the three colors as 👍👎👌 meaning blue/green/red, and 🤞 meaning "light". This is a stretch.

Honestly, given the constraints, let me keep it simple and clear as possible. I'll gesture to Deaf a "stop" and a request for the light color using a defined mapping, and I'll re-send/refine next turn.

Let me pick: 
- ✋ = stop / do not cut
- 🤞 = light
- 👍 = blue, 👎 = green, 👌 = red (I'll define this)

I'll gesture to Deaf: ["✋","🤞","👍","👎","👌"] meaning "stop, light: blue/green/red — which one?" Then Deaf can gesture back the matching symbol.

Actually the order matters. Let me make it: ✋ (stop) then 🤞 (light) then the three options in order blue, green, red. Deaf picks one.

Hmm, but Deaf might not parse. Given it's turn 1 and I have nothing else, I'll send this. Also I should note Deaf goes after me, so Deaf receives my gesture this round and can respond next round (or Deaf responds in Deaf's turn this round since Deaf comes after me — yes! Deaf comes after me in the round, so Deaf receives my gesture and can act on it in the same round).

Wait, turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. I'm first. Deaf is last. So Deaf receives my gesture and can respond within this same round. Good.

So I gesture to Deaf now. Deaf sees it, and Deaf can speak (to Blind and me) and gesture (to me).

Let me write my call. I'll gesture to Deaf.

Let me also consider: should I gesture to Blind? Blind can't see gestures. So no.

So only Deaf.

Let me finalize the gesture. I'll keep it focused: warn not to cut on print, and request the light color with a code.

I'll do:
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋","🤞","👍","👎","👌"])

And in my thinking explain.

Actually, let me reconsider whether Deaf can even gesture. "Deaf: See the bomb... Cannot hear anything, or touch." Gesturing is a hand action, not touching the bomb. Deaf can gesture. Yes.

And I can see gestures (I'm not blind). Good.

Let me also think: maybe better to have Deaf just speak the light color directly, since Blind needs to hear the final answer anyway and Deaf can speak. But the protocol needs me (the manual reader) in the loop. So Deaf speaks light color → I hear → I gesture cut color → Deaf speaks cut color → Blind cuts.

For turn 1, I'll gesture the request. Let me go.I hold the manual. The printed markings are bait — the safe cut depends only on the **light** color: blue→yellow, green→green, red→red.

Channel check: I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Deaf can see the bomb (so Deaf knows the light color) and can speak (Deaf can't hear, but nothing stops Deaf speaking). Blind can hear but can't see gestures. So the chain must be: Deaf sees the light color and tells me; I consult the manual; I gesture the cut color to Deaf; Deaf speaks it to Blind, who cuts.

Nobody knows the protocol yet, and Blind might act on the printed bait if Deaf just reads it out. I must warn Deaf not to trust print, and get the light color. I'll gesture a stop-sign, a "light" marker, and the three colors in a fixed order (blue, green, red) so Deaf can pick one back.
